concerns.text: The plan relies on a fully synthetic dataset to answer the research question about real-world correlations between musical preference and personality traits. Synthetic data can validate the pipeline but cannot provide evidence about actual associations, so the core claim of exploring the correlation cannot be fulfilled as stated.

No power analysis or sample‑size justification is provided. The plan caps the synthetic dataset at 10 k users, but there is no rationale showing this size is sufficient to detect the effect sizes of interest (e.g., |r| ≈ 0.3).

The analysis description mentions computing Pearson correlations, yet the contracts (analysis_output.schema.yaml) define fields for Spearman rho. This inconsistency leaves it unclear which correlation metric will be used, potentially affecting construct validity.

Only age, gender, and country are controlled as covariates. Other plausible confounds (e.g., education, socioeconomic status, overall music exposure) are not addressed, which may bias the estimated relationships.
